{{Short description|Theorem in functional analysis}}
In mathematics, '''Auerbach's lemma''', named after [[Herman Auerbach]], is a theorem in [[functional analysis]] which asserts that a certain property of [[Euclidean space]]s holds for general [[finite-dimensional]] [[normed vector space]]s.

== Statement ==
Let <math>(V, \|\cdot\|)</math> be an <math>n</math>-dimensional normed vector space. Then there exists a basis <math>\{e_{1}, \dots, e_{n}\}</math> of <math>V</math> such that  
<math>\|e_{i}\| = 1</math> and <math>\|e^{i}\| = 1</math> for <math>i = 1, \dots, n</math>,  
where <math>\{e^{1}, \dots, e^{n}\}</math> is a basis of <math>V^{*}</math> dual to <math>\{e_{1}, \dots, e_{n}\}</math>, i.e. <math>e^{i}(e_{j}) = \delta_{ij}</math>.

A basis with this property is called an Auerbach basis.

If <math>V</math> is an inner product space (or even infinite-dimensional Hilbert space) then this result is obvious as one may take for <math>\{e_{i}\}</math> any orthonormal basis of <math>V</math> (the dual basis is then <math>\{(e_{i}|\cdot)\}</math>).

=== Geometric formulation ===
An equivalent statement is the following: any centrally symmetric convex body in <math>\mathbf{R}^n</math> has a linear image which contains the unit cross-polytope (the unit ball for the <math>\ell_1^n</math> norm) and is contained in the unit cube (the unit ball for the <math>\ell_{\infty}^n</math> norm).

== Proof ==
By induction on the dimension <math>n</math>. Pick an arbitrary unit vector <math>e_n \in V</math>. Because the set of norm-1 points make up a convex symmetric body in <math>V</math>, there exists a hyperplane <math>P_n</math> supporting <math>V</math> at <math>e_n</math>. This is a consequence of the hyperplane separation theorem, which is a consequence of the Hahn–Banach theorem.

Now, define the dual vector <math>e^n \in V^*</math>, such that <math>\{x \in V : e^n(x) = 1\} = P_n</math>. That is, the contour surfaces of <math>e^n</math> are parallel to <math>P_n</math>.

Then, the subspace <math>\ker(e^n)</math> is a normed space of dimension <math>n-1</math>, and apply induction.

== Corollary ==
The lemma has a corollary with implications to approximation theory.

Let <math>V</math> be an <math>n</math>-dimensional subspace of a normed vector space <math>(X,\|\cdot\|)</math>. Then there exists a projection <math>P</math> of <math>X</math> onto <math>V</math> such that <math>\|P\| \le n</math>.

=== Proof ===
Let <math>\{e_{1}, \dots, e_{n}\}</math> be an Auerbach basis of <math>V</math> and <math>\{e^{1}, \dots, e^{n}\}</math> corresponding dual basis. By the Hahn–Banach theorem each <math>e^{i}</math> extends to <math>f^{i} \in X^*</math> such that  
<math>\|f^{i}\| = 1</math>.  
Now set  
<math>P(x) = \sum f^{i}(x) e_{i}</math>.  
It is easy to check that <math>P</math> is indeed a projection onto <math>V</math> and that <math>\|P\| \le n</math> (this follows from the triangle inequality).
